title: Explicit inverse candidate for the standing exceptional compositor
statement: For the finite purity datum P and separated finite-type k-morphisms f:X→Y, g:Y→S of finite-type schemes, and bounded constructible L on S, put V=f!g!L. Let H_h denote the standing Hom bijections of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], and alpha the canonical compact-support compositor of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Define b:V→(gf)!L by H_gf(alpha_V^{-1} ≫ H_g^{-1}(H_f^{-1}(id_V))). V is bounded below of etale origin, as are the required compact-support images, so each Hom bijection is on its stated domain. This uses precisely the standing choices of [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition].

lean.statement:
def standingExceptionalCompositionInverse (P : WeilConjectures.PurityFiniteSetting.{u})
    {X Y S : Scheme.{u}}
    [X.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [Y.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [S.Over (Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (S ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [QuasiCompact (S ↘ Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ S)
    [f.IsOver (Spec (.of P.field.k))] [g.IsOver (Spec (.of P.field.k))]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g]
